knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says an environmental claim does not replace the label and SDS, and a product that needs more use can waste resources. The label, SDS, surface and total effect are the first check. A claim on the front of the bottle (option 0) and a lower price (option 2) do not test effectiveness or safety.
The lesson says never to reduce a required protection or disinfection step to save resources. More accurate dosing (option 0) and travel grouping (option 2) are listed as valid reductions.
The lesson lists products, water and energy, waste, the fuel used for travel, packaging and materials, and wash water as points where service work affects the environment.

practicalCriteria: Learner walks through a supplied job and lists the products, water, energy, waste, travel and materials used.
Learner selects one practical reduction and checks it against the label, safety controls and quality standard before adopting it.
Learner records a trade-off where an environmental choice conflicts with a safety or quality choice, with the safety choice taken first.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Environmental reduction log with change, measure, trade-off and review date
stopWorkCriteria: Learner reduces a protection or disinfection step to save resources
Learner chooses a product for an environmental claim without checking its hazards or effectiveness
